title: Package management on Windows, Linux, and macOS

spans.alt: Package management on Windows, Linux, and macOS
spans.caption: A diagram of the lesson’s key ideas

spans.text: A package manager helps find, install, update, and remove applications from trusted sources. It can also track software dependencies. On a work computer, use approved sources and follow organization policy.

WinGet is a Windows command-line tool for finding, installing, upgrading, and removing applications. Verify the package ID; similar names can refer to different sources. If a command requests administrator access, check why and confirm your authority.

On systems such as Debian and Ubuntu, APT manages packages from configured repositories. Refreshing the package list does not by itself upgrade installed applications; a separate upgrade command is used. Review the proposed changes, especially if essential packages would be removed.

Update App Store applications through the App Store. Homebrew is a widely used, separately installed package manager for macOS; install it only by following its official instructions. The `brew` command commonly manages developer tools and other packages.
Choose the correct package name in these examples. Search first, then install; review the planned changes before upgrading. Commands are examples and can vary by operating-system version.

spans.code:
Windows (WinGet):
winget search <name>
winget install <package-id>
winget upgrade <package-id>
winget uninstall <package-id>

Ubuntu/Debian (APT):
sudo apt update
sudo apt upgrade
sudo apt install <package>
sudo apt remove <package>

macOS (Homebrew):
brew search <name>
brew install <formula>
brew upgrade <formula>
brew uninstall <formula>

spans.text: Install applications only from official or organization-approved sources. Updates can fix security weaknesses, but plan them around important work. Before removing software, consider its effect on user data and other applications; ask the support team if unsure.
